propositions: The test kills its pytest-xdist worker on macOS py3.13 due to exceeding the 300s per-test timeout budget: measured 91.6s idle, 504.8s under CPU saturation
pytest-timeout's thread method calls os._exit(1) from a timer thread, causing worker process death with no traceback or assertion output instead of a normal test failure
The test walks 884 renderable units each rendered twice (~1768 pandoc spawns) in a single monolithic loop, making per-test cost unbounded and load-dependent
Chunking the test with fixed-size batches (_EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK=40) bounds cost structurally so corpus growth adds cases rather than extending any single case duration
All 884 units remain compared byte-for-byte against the oracle with real pandoc; chunking only distributes work across xdist workers without weakening the equivalence property
